# CANDIDATE: RIBBON_PINCH_MEAN_REVERSION

**Filed:** 2026-07-09
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)
**Type:** new_trigger
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

When the EMA ribbon (8,21,34) contracts tightly (width < 0.001) and price trades outside the ribbon, a mean‑reversion to the ribbon midpoint is likely. This edge exists because a squeezed ribbon indicates low volatility and impending expansion, often reverting to the average cost basis represented by the ribbon midpoint.

## Mechanism

Compute EMA_fast (8), EMA_mid (21), EMA_slow (34) on the 5‑minute chart. Ribbon width = (EMA_fast - EMA_slow) / EMA_mid. If width < 0.001 AND price > EMA_slow (price above the ribbon) → go short; if price < EMA_fast (price below the ribbon) → go long. Entry is at the close of the candle that satisfies the condition. Exit: chart‑stop at the opposite ribbon edge (i.e., for a short, stop if price closes above EMA_fast; for a long, stop if price closes below EMA_slow). TP1 at 1R (risk‑reward 1:1) measured from entry to the chart‑stop distance. Runner trail at 1.5×ATR(14) from the highest high (long) or lowest low (short) after entry. Additionally, only trade when VIX < 20, time between 10:00‑14:00 ET, and |price‑VWAP| < 0.5×ATR(14) to ensure ranging conditions; avoid strong trends where price > VWAP + 1.5×ATR for >20 consecutive minutes.
